messages:
tony: FYI CI perf regression after the infra bump (driver 535.86.05) + PyTorch 2.2.1 rollout. Small-batch (bs=1, seq=64) 95p latency jumped from ~40ms to ~120ms on A100 canaries. Repro steps below.

nisha: ugh. is this the nightly that also pulled a runtime merge? or just the libs?

miguel: link to failing CI: https://ci.redwood.dev/builds/4421 — shows `latency-regression-check` failed on the canary cluster. perf-bot posted summary earlier: 95p +190% for small seq.

perf-bot: [automated] Regression detected in job latency-regression-check: metric=token_latency_95p, delta=+190%, p-value=0.002, group=A100-small-batch

tony: I ran a microbench on a repro node. Observed that kernel dispatch changed for fp16 matmuls — previously we hit `triton_mm_fp16_fast` kernels; now we see `triton_mm_fp16_shared_spill` with large global mem traffic. nvprof summary attached inline:  
```
GPU kernels:  triton_mm_fp16_shared_spill : 78%  (global mem loads >>)
previous run: triton_mm_fp16_fast : 86% (low global mem)
```

miguel: can you paste the exact command you used to repro?

tony: repro steps:
```
# on a canary with driver 535.86.05 and pytorch==2.2.1
docker run --rm --gpus all -it \ 
  --env TRITON_LOG_LEVEL=info \ 
  redwood/runtime-perf:canary /bin/bash -c "python microbench/matmul_bench.py --dtype fp16 --seq 64 --batch 1 --iters 500"
```
I also captured a triton dump with `TRITON_DUMP_KERNELS=1` — the dispatch table shows a new path: `matmul_v2` preferred over `matmul_legacy` after the merge.

nisha: so two moving pieces: driver & pytorch upgrade, plus we rolled a runtime change that prefers matmul_v2. Could be kernel selection + new driver scheduling interacting. can you bisect runtime?

tony: did a quick bisect, isolating runtime: reverted the `runtime/opt:prefer-matmul-v2` merge + kept driver and pytorch bumped — latency goes back to ~42ms. So runtime change is the proximate cause.

miguel: good catch. any idea why matmul_v2 regresses on A100 specifically? maybe different shared-memory footprint triggers spills.

tony: profiling shows matmul_v2 uses higher shared memory per CTA which reduces occupancy on A100 compute capability and bigger SM shared config, leading to increased global memory traffic on small batches. On smaller seq/batch, the lower occupancy matters more. For long seq throughput it's neutral or slightly better.

nisha: does matmul_v2 still win for large batch workloads? if yes, we could gate it behind heuristics (seq/batch threshold).

tony: exactly — currently the heuristic is coarse (prefer v2 for fp16 if shape >= X) but the merge changed thresholds to prefer v2 more aggressively. Quick fix: revert the merge or tighten the selector to require seq>=128 or batch>=4.

miguel: can we hotfix via env override so we don't have to revert runtime on master? e.g., `REDWOOD_FORCE_MATMUL=legacy` or something?

tony: I added `REDWOOD_FORCE_MATMUL=legacy` flag to the runtime (local branch) and tested — it restores prior 95p. I'll open a patch to add an env var and roll to canaries while we fix selector.

perf-bot: [automated] new PR 6403 opened by tony: `runtime: add REDWOOD_FORCE_MATMUL to override matmul selector` — triggered microbench matrix.

nisha: schedule: we should block the driver+torch rollout until canaries confirm no regression. For now, block the fleet rollout and push the env var to canaries.

miguel: agree. also add a short-term runtime revert-ready PR in case the env flag misses something.

sre-bot: Action items: pin driver on remaining infra nodes to 525.x, apply `REDWOOD_FORCE_MATMUL=legacy` to canaries, and mark rollout blocked in the rollout tracker: https://infra.redwood/rollouts/857.

tony: I'll send the env change + test plan in PR and will follow up with perf traces. Also adding a unit test that asserts selector picks legacy for (bs=1,seq<=96) on A100.

nisha: thanks — can you also dump the triton kernel metadata (shared mem usage / regs / occupancy) and attach to PR so ML infra folks can tune kernels?

tony: will do. quick note: this only triggered with driver 535 in our canaries; we didn't see it on 525, but since the runtime change made v2 preferred the regression surfaced. So it's a compatibility edge between kernel resource assumptions and the new driver/pt build.

miguel: sound plan. once env override is in canaries and CI microbench passes, we can decide to revert or patch selector. For rollout blocker: until env override is in place, mark rollout as blocked.

nisha: ping-ing eng leads for awareness : @eng-platform @eng-ml — this is perf-sensitive; we need coordinator for release notes.

miguel: ack. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: [automated] follow-up: regression triage assigned to @tony and @miguel.

tony: I'll ship the env-override PR in the next hour and start the selector patch. Will update thread when canaries green.

miguel: thanks — and please add the lightweight reproducer script to the repo so QE can run on other hw variants.

tony: added. test command in PR.

sre-bot: Blocking note set on rollout 857. last_message_ts=1795007600

nisha: thanks team, good triage.
